subject: general
question: A man travels non-stop over a certain distance at an average speed of 60 km/h. With stoppages his speed reduces to 50 km/h. How many minutes per hour does he stop?
solution:
**Given:**

A man travels non-stop at 60 km/h, but with stoppages his speed reduces to 50 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Time stopped per hour = (Difference in speeds / Original speed) × 60 minutes

**Calculations:**

Difference in speeds = 60 - 50 = 10 km/h

Time stopped per hour = (10 / 60) × 60 minutes

⇒ Time stopped per hour = 10 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is option (1) 10 minutes.**
